design: One deployment candidate: five-fold normal-calibration ensemble of the existing three-column score. No comparisons of seeds, fold counts, aggregation, transformation, threshold or cutoffs.
features_and_score: Using 1-based columns 2, 3, 6, learn per-column Yeo-Johnson transformations, median and Q10-Q90 scaling on each fitting subset. Score = max(z2,0)*max(-z6,0)/(1+max(z3,0)), the distance from its fitted zero normal median.
data: Read only the course normal train CSV, globally deduplicate exact six-feature rows retaining first occurrence and original relative order. Final fit on all 1782 unique normals.
ensemble: Five-fold sklearn KFold, shuffle=True, random_state=42. Each of five estimators fits on four folds and computes a distinct tau on the held-out normal fold. alpha=0.005; tau = ceil((n_cal+1)*(1-alpha))-th smallest normal calibration score. Normalize each test score by that fold's positive tau. Score and decision both use median(s_j/tau_j) with strictly >1 identifying an anomaly. No p-value aggregation.
normal_validation: Five outer folds on all unique normals with shuffle=True, random_state=1126, independently of the inner five. Predict each outer normal only by submodels fitted and calibrated entirely within the other outer folds. For comparison, the fixed single-split three-column control fits on ~80% of each outer training subset and calibrates on the rest (ceil(20%), seed 42). Each model is scored on precisely the same held-out rows and simulated perturbations.
simulation: Use the three frozen round-one marginal-tail/shift profiles (balanced, second dominant, sixth dominant), changing columns 2 and 6 in the held-out normal rows while retaining the original third and other columns. Same seed family 900+10*zero-based outer fold+zero-based scenario; compare counts and fold-to-fold variability. Artificial sensitivity does not estimate true disease detection.
decision: The training comparison is descriptive; there is one deployable ensemble with no selection or fallback based on these diagnostics. Fit on all unique normals and freeze the joblib artifact, five thresholds and source hashes before a single course-test evaluation. Save scores and predictions before the separate evaluation-label read. Do not change the rule in response to test labels.
limits: The feature choice and alpha inherit historical course-test selection. The cross-fitted ensemble decision has no asserted split-conformal coverage guarantee. Single-fold alpha remains a calibration working point. The course evaluation is exploratory.
